lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Rebuilt weekly carrier scorecards used by 6 regional managers to renegotiate contracts, cutting late deliveries from 11% to 7% in two quarters.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites; my redesign of the slotting rules was rolled out with the floor supervisors and 45 retrained pickers.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing, Python
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The résumé leads with an unrelated mechanic role, obscuring the product direction.
items.because: A recruiter sees it before the product-management internship.

items.says: Projects appear after Education, delaying the product work.
The dry-dock threshold has no comparison.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether it was an improvement or a schedule target.

items.says: The inspection phrase gives no outcome for the maintenance records.
The checkout-test bullet shifts from a past-tense action to a gerund.
The bullet misstates the conventional RICE Reach measure.
items.because: Reach estimates people or users affected over a defined period, not support tickets closed.

items.says: The bullet does not name the roadmap choice.
items.because: A reader cannot tell which initiative was selected or why it mattered.

items.says: The RICE explanation is dense.
items.because: It may slow readers unfamiliar with the framework.

items.says: The loss analysis gives no estimate or comparison.
items.because: A reader cannot judge the size of the opportunity or what the analysis found.

items.says: The selected roadmap priority is buried and unnamed.
items.because: The long list of methods delays the decision without saying what was chosen.

items.says: Session-level randomization does not support describing the lift as an effect on customers.
items.because: Repeat customers can contribute multiple sessions or experience both variants.

items.says: The description of the reported lift is awkward and unclear.
items.because: Readers must work out what the five-point figure refers to.

items.says: The checkout test and five-point lift repeat the preceding bullet.
items.because: Separating the design from its result makes the entry repetitive.

items.says: The bullet uses a first-person possessive.
The passive rollout wording obscures your role.
The duration is phrased more lengthily than needed.
The driver-hour savings are buried after a long list of tasks.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the strongest result.

items.says: The list of tasks makes their connection to the savings unclear.
items.because: It is unclear which work drove the 1,800-hour result.

items.says: “Taking over” makes the contract-negotiation action wordier than a direct description.
The launch claim does not identify the product or rollout work you owned.
items.because: A reader cannot connect the impact to a specific product-lead contribution.

items.says: The explanation of “surplus-food” adds words without adding much information.
The stated 150% increase is wrong; the increase is 187.5%.
items.because: The increase of 750 users is 187.5% of the starting 400.

items.says: The bullet repeats the change with both before-and-after figures and a percentage.
The change from 75% to 95% is 20 percentage points, not a 20% relative increase.
items.because: Relative to 75%, the increase is about 26.7%.

items.says: The bullet states the change twice.
items.because: “By 20%” repeats the before-and-after rates.

items.says: The savings estimate lacks a baseline cost or key assumption.
items.because: A reader cannot assess what supports the $2.4M estimate.

items.says: The analytical inputs behind the model are unnamed.
items.because: “Based on the model” does not show what informed it.

items.says: The pilot outcome repeats the next bullet.
items.because: The repetition splits the estimate from its outcome.

items.says: The intake-form bullet uses passive voice.
items.because: It hides who mapped the intake and shortened the form.

items.says: The intake-form bullet gives no result of the change.
items.because: Adoption does not show whether intake became faster, more complete or otherwise better.

items.says: The pilot approval is buried after the audience list.
items.because: That placement delays the clearest result for a scanning reader.
